Which update does a risk model need? Localization with the updated-model reference

Source: R/localize_update.R
localize.update.Rd

Checks frozen predictions on validation data and names the parts of the misfit that are present, so that the verdict points to the update the model needs. The four parts and their bases are those of localize.external; what changes is the reference. Each part is tested against the model already updated for the simpler parts:

INTERCEPTagainst the frozen model \(p\) (Monte Carlo)
SLOPEagainst the intercept update \(a + \eta\)
LINKagainst the logistic recalibration \(a + b\eta\)
COVagainst the flexible recalibration ns(eta, 4)

with \(\eta = \mathrm{logit}(p)\). Except for INTERCEPT this is a parametric bootstrap: B outcome vectors are drawn from the fitted update, the update is refitted to each draw, and each part's bases are projected off that update's own directions with its own fitted weights. The hypothesis of each test is therefore "this part is zero, whatever the simpler parts are": a large error in overall risk or slope is absorbed by the update and cannot inflate the tests of the more demanding parts. This makes localize.update() the function to use after transport to another population, where localize.external can name a rung that is too high.

Usage

localize.update(
  y,
  p,
  X,
  B = 199L,
  alpha = 0.05,
  naming = c("holm", "bonferroni"),
  cov_df = 5,
  cluster = NULL,
  tau = 0,
  main = TRUE,
  seed = NULL,
  plot = interactive()
)

Arguments

y

0/1 outcomes.

p

the frozen predicted probabilities, one per outcome, in \([0, 1]\); values of exactly 0 or 1 are moved to 1e-10 and 1 - 1e-10.

X

a numeric matrix or data frame of covariates, one row per outcome, without missing values or constant columns. At least one column; COV needs two.

B

number of reference draws for each part; each p-value lies on a grid of 1 / (B + 1).

alpha

familywise level.

naming

"holm" (the default) or "bonferroni".

cov_df

as in localize.external.

cluster

optional vector of centre labels, one per outcome.

tau

the standard deviation of the centre effect on the logit scale; used with cluster.

main

if TRUE, COV includes the main-effects member; see Details.

seed

optional integer, passed to set.seed() before the reference draws. The random number stream of the session is restored on exit.

plot

if TRUE, draw the verdict with plot.gof_localize. The default draws it in an interactive session and not in scripts, simulations or examples.

Value

An object of class "gof_localize", as described in localize.external. Here intersection holds the Bonferroni test of each set of parts, whose closure is Holm's procedure; draws is the smallest number of usable draws over the parts (a refit that fails is dropped).

Details

With this reference COV has a fourth member beside those of localize.external: the main effects of the covariates, so that a changed coefficient, of a binary covariate too, has a test of its own. Risks pooled by cross-validation are not fully frozen: their coefficients differ from fold to fold, and the main-effects member responds to that difference even when the form of the model is right. Use main = FALSE for such risks, and check the error rate by repeating the refits in simulated data.

The parts are named by Holm's correction of their p-values (the default) or by Bonferroni's.

When the validation data come from several centres, outcomes within a centre are correlated and the plain reference names INTERCEPT too often. Give cluster and tau, the standard deviation of a centre random effect on the logit scale, usually estimated by a random-intercept model; every reference draw then carries a new effect for each centre.

Reading a verdict

Act on the highest group named, in the order INTERCEPT < SLOPE < LINK < COV: it points to the lightest update that repairs the model (Steyerberg et al. 2004).

INTERCEPTupdate the intercept
SLOPElogistic recalibration \(a + b\eta\)
LINKflexible recalibration \(f(\eta)\) or another link
COVrevise the model, even if other groups are named too

When nothing is named, no misfit was detected; that verdict is limited by the sample size. When the miscalibration is gross, as after transport to another population, a large error on the logit scale also bends the probability curve, so the named rung can be too high. Then split the validation data at random, reach the verdict and update on one half, and test the updated (frozen) model on the other half with this function.

References

Ebrahim, E. K., Hussein, O. A. E.-A. and El-Kotory, A. (2026). Which update does a clinical risk model need? Localization of misfit in logistic risk models. Submitted. Reproduction materials: doi:10.5281/zenodo.24025418

Holm, S. (1979). A simple sequentially rejective multiple test procedure. Scandinavian Journal of Statistics, 6(2), 65–70.

Vergouwe, Y., Nieboer, D., Oostenbrink, R., Debray, T. P. A., Murray, G. D., Kattan, M. W., Koffijberg, H., Moons, K. G. M. and Steyerberg, E. W. (2017). A closed testing procedure to select an appropriate method for updating prediction models. Statistics in Medicine, 36(28), 4529–4539. doi:10.1002/sim.7179

See also

localize.size for the size of each part; localize.external for the frozen-model reference; localize.gof for a fitted model checked on its own data.

Examples

set.seed(1)
n <- 500
X <- data.frame(x1 = rnorm(n), x2 = rnorm(n))
p <- plogis(-0.5 + 0.8 * X$x1 + 0.6 * X$x2)                     # the published model
y <- rbinom(n, 1, plogis(-0.7 + qlogis(p) + 0.8 * X$x1 * X$x2))  # new patients
localize.update(y, p, X, B = 49, seed = 1)   # B = 49 to keep the example fast; use 199 or more
#> 
#> Localization of misfit: updated-model reference
#> 
#> data:     y and p (n = 500)
#> setting:  external validation of frozen predictions
#> reference: updated model, 49 draws
#> 
#> p-values by group (alone, and adjusted by Holm over the groups):
#>            alone adjusted named
#> INTERCEPT 0.0200   0.0800      
#> SLOPE     0.5000   0.5000      
#> LINK      0.0200   0.0800      
#> COV       0.0200   0.0800      
#> 
#> groups named (Holm over the groups) at FWER 0.05: none
#> recommended update: keep the model; no misfit detected (the verdict is limited
#>   by the sample size)
#>
